0912Medicine

KlinikeBench

anon-caa-neurips/klinikebench

Act as the clinician: interview an LLM-simulated patient, use chart, lab and imaging tools through a clinic CLI, and record a diagnosis.

Open on Hugging FaceHow to run it

Good for

  • clinical agent evaluation
  • RL on consultation tasks (SFT then GRPO)
  • held-out evaluation split

Reward

How it is scored
Mixed
Signal
Graded, 0 to 1

Four gates are scored (diagnosis, required tools, parameterised actions, LLM-judged must-ask coverage); outcome mode gives 1 only if all pass, multigate gives a weighted fraction.

How to run it

1. From the cardcopied from the publisher's own instructions

export OPENAI_API_KEY=...                    # patient simulator + must-ask judge
harbor run --repo https://huggingface.co/datasets/anon-caa-neurips/klinikebench \
  -a terminus-2 -m <provider/model>

2. Get the filesthe whole repository, to a local folder

hf download anon-caa-neurips/klinikebench --repo-type dataset --local-dir klinikebench

3. Check it with Harborcommon pattern, not from this card

# the oracle agent runs the reference solution, so no model is called
harbor run --repo https://huggingface.co/datasets/anon-caa-neurips/klinikebench --agent oracle

If every task passes, the environment works on your machine. Then swap in your own agent and model. Some repositories keep the tasks in a subfolder; the card says where.

Framework documentation: Harbor. Needs: Docker and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for patient simulator and judge.

Evidence

A scripted oracle scores 1.0; the paper trains Qwen3-4B with SFT then GRPO on 283 tasks and evaluates on 50 held out.

As reported by the publisher. We have not reproduced it.
